entry_door: signed-in supabase-js (admin@admin.com), custom.table_declare / custom.field_declare / custom.record_write / custom.record_update
limitations: No client-callable door can declare a generic table-to-table relation field. custom.field_declare exposes 13 parity types but only two relation shortcuts (member -> Person kernel, attachment -> File kernel); there is no parity type for a relation that points at a table the caller names. A direct custom.record_write into the field kernel with type=relation and an arbitrary relation_target is refused: 23514 FLD-13, "write a column through custom.field_declare ... custom.record_write stores a plain record and its class defaults to record". Worked around by adding denormalized text fields (client_site_name, pickup_ref_link) instead of real relations.

As a direct consequence, a ROLLUP field (parity_type=rollup, config.via/agg/of) cannot be declared either, because it requires an existing relation field on the same table to read through (store's own words: "config.via names a field of the SAME table, by key") and none could be created. Worked around with a manually-computed total_weight_lbs_manual number field written by the client on every weight-entry write, instead of a live rollup.

A table's declared fields array can be updated via custom.record_update to add a field key that has no matching Field record in the field kernel, and the store accepts this with no cross-check - the guard only fires the other direction (field_declare/record_write refuses a field whose key is not already in the table's fields array). This left an abandoned phantom field name in the fields array of pickups, weights_by_material and certificates_of_destruction in this organization.
